belongs_to: Perfect Squares and Odd Numbers: 'adding consecutive odd numbers starting from 1 gives consecutive square numbers, as shown below' (equations on the left, dot square with red L-lines on the right)

(red results 1, 4, 9, 16, 25, 36). RIGHT: a 6 × 6 array of 36 black filled dots (6 rows, 6 columns, equal spacing). Six nested red inverted-L lines are drawn over it; each L is a red horizontal stroke above a row plus a red vertical stroke to the right of a column, open on the left and bottom; the vertical strokes run down to just below the bottom row. From outside to inside: (1) L above row 1 and right of column 6, enclosing row 1 (6 dots) and column 6 rows 2-6 (5 dots) = 11 dots; (2) L above row 2 and right of column 5, enclosing row 2 columns 1-5 (5 dots) and column 5 rows 3-6 (4 dots) = 9 dots; (3) L above row 3 and right of column 4: row 3 columns 1-4 and column 4 rows 4-6 = 7 dots; (4) L above row 4 and right of column 3: row 4 columns 1-3 and column 3 rows 5-6 = 5 dots; (5) L above row 5 and right of column 2: row 5 columns 1-2 and column 2 row 6 = 3 dots; (6) innermost L above row 6 and right of column 1 enclosing only the bottom-left dot = 1 dot. The L-lines are nested like corners of squares 6, 5, 4, 3, 2, 1; no numbers are written inside the dot array.

belongs_to: 'Do you remember this pattern from Grade 6? The picture below explains why each subsequent inverted L gives the next odd number' (visual proof)

belongs_to: Figure it Out Q9: 'How many tiny squares are there in the following picture? Write the prime factorisation of the number of tiny squares.'
description: A large rectangular (almost square, about 597 × 595 px) mid-green panel holding 9 rows × 9 columns = 81 white tiles in a checkerboard alternation of two tile types, with thin green lines cutting the white tiles into small cells. Type D = a white square turned 45° (diamond) cut by green lines into a 5 × 5 lattice of 25 tiny squares (all 41 diamonds identical). Type S = an upright white square (about 47 px, smaller than a diamond) cut by one or two vertical and one or two horizontal green lines placed unevenly into 4, 6 or 9 cells: S4 = 2 × 2 cells (4 cells; the two dividers sit at about 40% and 60% along the sides); S6 = 6 cells, 2 columns × 3 rows in rows 1 and 5 (outer strips narrow, middle wide), but 3 columns × 2 rows in the other rows; S9 = 3 × 3 cells with narrow outer strips and a wide middle strip. Rows read left to right (D diamond, number = cells of the upright square): row 1: D, S6(2 columns × 3 rows), D, S9, D, S6(2 × 3), D, S9, D. row 2: S4, D, S4, D, S6(3 columns × 2 rows), D, S6(3 × 2), D, S4. row 3: D, S4, D, S6(3 × 2), D, S4, D, S6(3 × 2), D. row 4: same as row 2 (S4, D, S4, D, S6, D, S6, D, S4). row 5: same as row 1. row 6: same as row 2. row 7: same as row 3. row 8: same as row 2. row 9: same as row 3. Odd rows (1, 3, 5, 7, 9) start and end with a diamond (5 diamonds + 4 uprights); even rows (2, 4, 6, 8) start and end with an upright square (4 diamonds + 5 uprights). Counts verified by image component counting: 41 diamonds × 25 = 1025 cells; 40 upright squares = 18 with 4 cells (72) + 18 with 6 cells (108) + 4 with 9 cells (36) = 216 cells; total 1025 + 216 = 1241 white cells (1241 = 17 × 73). No numbers or labels on the panel.
unclear: The upright squares are cut into unequal rectangles (not equal tiny squares), so whether their cells count as 'tiny squares' is not clear from the picture.
The book gives no printed answer for Q9 (the printed solutions on pdf p.20-22 stop at Q8), so 1241 is my own count of all white cells and is not confirmed by the book.
